admission.justification: The install step alone says nothing about what a dashboard start does to a running host; the start's start-only rule alone says nothing about where the release and the Node come from; and the no-stop rule alone says nothing about visibility or the one authority. Only together do they promise that two commands a user runs bring up the build's host and never take a running one down.

guarantee: One build's install brings exactly that build's host — its release, its complete package lock, its plugin and a Node the product fetches and verifies itself — every dashboard start makes sure that host runs, one installation-wide authority names it, and neither the install nor a dashboard start or stop removes a host that is running. Release changes stay build-owned; when a required live-host transition is needed — a different contract, or a same-contract listen, start-only-setting, Node or package change — the explicit terminal provision (`agents-remember paseo provision --config <file>`) performs it, and a different build is not a necessary condition for that transition. Public status exposes an observed executable mismatch with the contract Node and its existing explicit provision remedy without changing the host; successful explicit provision reports the earlier sibling product Node folder as no longer used by that host while retaining its files.
title: One build-owned host lifecycle
